purpose: W7 Compute limits: current figures and dates for each limit, one sourced reading each; reuse of series_v3 noted in series_v3 fields. Round 2: readings capped at 28 words; primary sources replace blogs where one exists; secondary: true marks items resting on press estimates or vendor claims.
schema: group, id, label, figure, unit, date, source {title, url}, reading, notes, series_v3, sources[], secondary (bool, optional)

items.label: Global data centre electricity use
items.date: 2026 (IEA Key Questions on Energy and AI; 2025 reading)

source.title: IEA: Key Questions on Energy and AI, executive summary

items.reading: Data centres used about 485 TWh in 2025, 17 percent more than in 2024. The IEA projects 950 TWh by 2030, near 3 percent of world demand.

items.label: US interconnection queue, generation waiting and median wait

source.title: LBNL: Queued Up, 2025 edition

items.reading: At end 2024, 1,400 GW of generation waited in US grid queues. Projects finished since 2018 took a median of more than four years from request to operation.

items.label: Largest announced single AI campus

source.title: OpenAI: OpenAI joins PORTS-Pike project

items.reading: OpenAI has agreed to secure about 8 GW of power for computing equipment at Ohio's PORTS-Pike campus in Pike County; its first 800 MW arrives in 2028.
items.notes: Announced, not built. The Cincinnati Enquirer (24 Aug 2026) reports 10 GW of site power and the Energy Secretary's "largest in the world" claim; OpenAI's page makes no size claim.

sources.title: Cincinnati Enquirer: OpenAI to build world's biggest AI data center in Ohio
Inside the Datacenter: Summer of the Gigawatt

items.label: TSMC CoWoS packaging capacity (press estimate)

source.title: TrendForce: TSMC reportedly targets 22% 2nm capacity boost by mid-2027; CoWoS to double by 2028

items.reading: Press estimates put TSMC's CoWoS capacity, its step packaging GPU dies with memory, near 130,000 wafers a month by end 2026, with demand 10 to 20 percent above supply.
items.notes: TSMC publishes no CoWoS capacity figure. TrendForce relays Taiwanese press estimates (Economic Daily News citing institutional investors); the June 2026 item gives 120,000 to 140,000 wafers per month for 2026.

sources.title: TrendForce, 15 Jun 2026: CoWoS supply-demand gap narrowing

items.label: High-bandwidth memory market share, Q2 2026

source.title: Counterpoint Research: Global DRAM and HBM market share, quarterly

items.reading: SK hynix held half of HBM revenue in Q2 2026, down from 64 percent a year earlier, as Samsung climbed to one third.
items.notes: Quarterly table on the page: SK hynix 64/56/57/58/50, Samsung 15/23/22/21/33, Micron 21/21/21/21/18 for Q2 2025 to Q2 2026.

items.label: NVIDIA accelerator cadence

figure.Vera Rubin: full production, GTC Taipei June 2026; shipments from autumn 2026

source.title: NVIDIA Newsroom: NVIDIA Vera Rubin ramps into full production to power agentic AI factories worldwide

items.reading: NVIDIA said in June 2026 that Vera Rubin is in full production, one year after Blackwell Ultra, with shipments from autumn and a new chip architecture each year.
items.notes: Rubin Ultra and Feynman timing is from NVIDIA's GTC roadmap as summarised by SourceBySpec (Sep 2026); SemiAnalysis reported in July 2026 that the Kyber rack for Rubin Ultra slipped to 2028, which NVIDIA disputed.

sources.title: SourceBySpec: NVIDIA GPU roadmap 2026 to 2028

items.label: US advanced-chip export control scope today

source.title: Reuters Practical Law: What's the latest with semiconductor export controls

items.reading: Chips scoring at or above 1,600 on TPP, a performance measure, need licences for export to the Commerce Department's Country Groups D:1, D:4 and D:5, China included. Washington said in May 2025 it would not enforce Biden's worldwide-licensing AI Diffusion rule; China sales get case-by-case review.

sources.title: series_v3 chip_export_controls (15 dated actions)

items.label: China's domestic accelerators

source.title: Reuters: Chinese chipmakers claim nearly half of local market as Nvidia's lead shrinks, IDC

items.reading: IDC counts 1.65 million AI cards from Chinese makers in 2025, 41 percent of China's market, 812,000 of them Huawei's. Huawei plans one Ascend generation a year.
items.notes: Shipment counts are not comparable to NVIDIA units in performance.

sources.title: Huawei: Eric Xu keynote, HUAWEI CONNECT 2025 (Ascend roadmap)

items.label: Stock of public human text for training

source.title: Epoch AI: Will we run out of data?

items.reading: Epoch puts the usable stock of public human text near 300 trillion tokens and expects models to have used it all between 2026 and 2032, likely around 2028.

items.label: Synthetic data in a production pretraining mix (phi-4)

source.title: Microsoft: Phi-4 technical report (arXiv 2412.08905)

items.reading: Microsoft's phi-4 pretrained on about 10 trillion tokens, 40 percent of them synthetic: one published case of a model trained partly on model output.
items.notes: One published example; frontier labs do not publish their synthetic shares.

items.label: Big four hyperscaler capital expenditure

source.title: Amazon.com announces fourth quarter results (2025)

items.reading: Company filings put 2025 capital spending near $360 billion across Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet and Meta. Guidance given in early 2026 adds up to $605 to 635 billion.
items.notes: Four firms, not five: no Oracle figure. Capex is total, not AI only. Alphabet's 2025 total did not fetch from a primary; CNBC reports the 2026 top end as more than double 2025, consistent with the $91.4 billion in the Meridian Report reconstruction. Meridian Report (Oct 2026) sums 2025 at $380 billion including finance leases and later-raised 2026 guidance at $720 to 745 billion.

Microsoft FY25 Q4 press release (cash flow statement)
Meta reports fourth quarter and full year 2025 results
CNBC: Alphabet Q4 2025 earnings

items.label: AI share of global venture funding

source.title: Crunchbase News: funding data, 2025

items.reading: About half of all venture dollars in 2025 went to AI companies, up from one third in 2024.

items.label: Algorithmic efficiency of pretraining

source.title: Epoch AI: Algorithmic progress in language models

items.reading: Compute needed to reach a given language-model score has halved about every eight months since 2012, software gains on top of hardware gains.

items.label: Cost of a fixed level of AI performance

source.title: Epoch AI: The plunging price of thought

items.reading: Since 2023, prices to reach a given benchmark score have fallen about 47 percent per quarter, or 13 times per year.

items.label: Largest known training run

source.title: Epoch AI: Data on Notable AI Models (CSV)

items.reading: Epoch's largest listed training run for 2026 is about 9.4 × 10^26 FLOP, double 2025's largest. Frontier compute has grown 4 to 5 times a year.
items.notes: Epoch estimates with stated confidence levels; growth rate from Epoch's May 2024 analysis (5.3x per year 2010 to 2024, 4.2x per year since 2018). Training power doubles yearly (Epoch, 2.1x per year; Grok 3 at about 110 MW).

sources.title: Epoch AI: Training compute of frontier AI models grows by 4-5x per year
Epoch AI: power required to train frontier models is doubling annually

items.label: Frontier API list price, input tokens (GPT-4 to GPT-5.2)

source.title: OpenAI API pricing (current) and vendor announcements, series_v3 api_price_frontier

items.reading: A million input tokens cost $30 for GPT-4 in March 2023 and $1.75 for GPT-5.2 on OpenAI's October 2026 list: 17 times cheaper.
items.notes: Settled pair, matching series_v3 api_price_frontier and the AI now row: GPT-4 at $30 to GPT-5.2 at $1.75, a 17-fold fall. GPT-5 launched at $1.25 in August 2025 (24-fold); other vendors listed in October 2026 at $2 (Gemini 3.1 Pro) and $4 (Claude Opus 5.5).

items.label: Largest context windows

source.title: Meta AI: The Llama 4 herd

items.reading: Meta's Llama 4 Scout advertises a 10-million-token context window, meaning how much text it can take in at once; commercial frontier models accept about one million tokens.
items.notes: Advertised windows, not measured effective context. Google's Gemini API model page states no input limit in its fetched text; the one-million figures come from the AI Intel Report comparison.

sources.title: AI Intel Report: LLM context window sizes by model (2026)

items.label: Fastest published inference speed (vendor claim)

source.title: Cerebras: Introducing Cerebras CS-4

items.reading: Cerebras serves one 120-billion-parameter open model at 3,000 tokens per second and frontier-size models above 1,000, by its own figures.
items.notes: Vendor claims; no independent benchmark page fetched (Artificial Analysis did not fetch).

sources.title: Cerebras inference page: gpt-oss-120B at 3,000 tokens per second

items.label: New AI PhDs, US and Canada

source.title: Stanford AI Index 2026: Education chapter

items.reading: New AI PhDs in the US and Canada rose 22 percent from 2022 to 2024; 65 percent went to industry, down from 77 percent in 2022.
items.notes: The chapter does not print the absolute counts in the extracted text (CRA Taulbee data, figures 7.2.7 and 7.2.8).

items.label: Researcher pay at the top

source.title: Levels.fyi: Anthropic software engineer salaries

items.reading: Levels.fyi medians for software engineers: $882,500 at Anthropic and $640,000 at OpenAI. Meta's package for one researcher was reported above $200 million.
items.notes: Self-reported submissions, small sample at Anthropic. The $200 million figure for Ruoming Pang is Bloomberg's, relayed by Reuters. Pin's $875,000 OpenAI median (Oct 2026) disagrees with the Levels.fyi page read directly.

sources.title: Levels.fyi: OpenAI software engineer salaries
Reuters, 26 Feb 2026: OpenAI hires Ruoming Pang from Meta

items.label: Power per rack

source.title: NVIDIA Technical Blog: NVIDIA 800 V HVDC architecture will power the next generation of AI factories

items.reading: NVIDIA describes current AI racks as exceeding 200 kW and is building 800-volt DC distribution for racks of 1 MW and beyond from 2027.
items.notes: NVIDIA gives no per-rack kW for GB200 NVL72 or Kyber. The 132 kW (GB200 NVL72) and 600 kW (Kyber) figures are from GR1D and Inside Deep Tech, secondary; SemiAnalysis reported Kyber slipping to 2028.

sources.title: GR1D: 800 VDC data centers and Vera Rubin, explained
Inside Deep Tech: Rubin Ultra and Kyber guide

items.label: TSMC process node roadmap (trade-press report of the 2026 symposium)

source.title: Semiconductor Engineering: TSMC Tech Symposium 2026, by the numbers

items.reading: Two-nanometre chips entered production in late 2025. TSMC's 2026 symposium showed A16 for 2027 and A14 for 2028, each step about two years apart.
items.notes: TSMC's own symposium press release did not fetch. Semiconductor Engineering reports the 2026 roadmap moved A16 to 2027; Fiisual's summary still lists 4Q26. 2nm capacity figure from TrendForce press estimates.

TrendForce, 14 Sep 2026: 2nm and CoWoS capacity

items.label: Accelerator compute per watt

source.title: NVIDIA datasheets; series_v3 flop_per_watt_datasheets

items.reading: Each watt buys about five times the dense FP16 compute it did in 2017, from 417 GFLOP/s per watt on V100 to 2,250 on B200.
